18	The three **File** items have no keyboard shortcut. Each opens a small sheet with a **Graphic:** pop-up.

20	## Rename Graphic
21	
22	Renaming a module changes its file name, and every clip drawn by it follows the new name, on the timeline and inside nests.
23	
24	<Steps>
25	
26	1. Choose **File ▸ Rename Graphic…**. The sheet opens on the selected clip's module when one clip is selected, otherwise on the first module.
27	
28	2. Pick the module from **Graphic:** if it's a different one. The **New name:** field starts with the chosen module's name, and changes when you pick another.
29	
30	3. Type the new name and choose **Rename**.
31	
32	</Steps>
33	
34	<Shot
35	  name="15b-rename-graphic-sheet.sheet"
36	  alt="The Rename Graphic sheet. A paragraph explains that every clip follows the new name and how to rename back. Graphic: is a pop-up reading lower-third, and New name: is a field holding the same name. Bottom left, small grey text reads lowercase letters, digits and -. Bottom right are Cancel and a dimmed Rename."
37	/>
38	
39	A name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit, and at most 63 characters. **Rename** stays dimmed until the name isn't empty and differs from the current one.
40	
41	The module's [kept versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/#kept-versions) move with it. If the new name belonged to a deleted module, the two sets of versions join under that name. Past 10, the oldest are dropped for good, and those are the deleted module's.
42	
43	The item is dimmed in a project with no graphics and while a nest is open, because a rename reaches every clip in the project. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> first.
44	
45	## Undo a rename
46	
47	When a clip uses the module, a rename is one undo step, **Rename Graphic**. **Edit ▸ Undo** puts the clips back and moves the module's file back to its old name with them, and **Edit ▸ Redo** moves both forward again.
48	
49	A module no clip uses makes no undo step. To go back, rename it again.
50	
51	Frame Job remembers the last 32 renames in a project to do this. An undo further back than that can leave a clip naming a module that has no file, and the clip draws the [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card).
52	
53	## Delete Graphic
54	
55	Deleting removes a module that no clip uses. Its code is kept, so you can bring it back.
56	
57	<Steps>
58	
59	1. Delete the clips drawn by the module, or switch them to another one. See [Switch clips to another module](#switch-clips-to-another-module).
60	
61	2. Choose **File ▸ Delete Graphic…**. The sheet always opens on the first module in the list.
62	
63	3. Pick the module from **Graphic:** and choose **Delete**.
64	
65	</Steps>
66	
67	<Shot
68	  name="15c-delete-graphic-sheet.sheet"
69	  alt="The Delete Graphic sheet. A paragraph explains that a graphic clips still use cannot be deleted, that its code is kept so Restore Graphic Version brings it back, and that deleting is not an Undo step. Graphic: is a pop-up reading lower-third. Bottom right are Cancel and a blue Delete."
70	/>
71	
72	**Delete** is the only confirmation. There's no second question, and deleting isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited.
73	
74	Clips count wherever they are, on the timeline or in a nest. Fonts and pictures are left alone. The item is dimmed in a project with no graphics.
75	
76	## Switch clips to another module
77	
78	The inspector can't point clips at a different module that already exists. **Duplicate as New Graphic…** only switches them to a new copy. To move clips to an existing module, delete the clips and [insert that module](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) again, or ask an agent to do it.
79	
80	## Restore Graphic Version
81	
82	Restoring puts back the newest kept version of a module's code, and it works on deleted modules too.
83	
84	<Steps>
85	
86	1. Choose **File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…**. The sheet opens on the selected clip's module when one clip is selected and that module has a kept version, otherwise on the first in the list.
87	
88	2. Pick the module from **Graphic:**. The pop-up lists every name with a kept version, and a deleted one reads like `lower-third (deleted)`. Under it, the sheet says how many are kept, such as "3 versions kept".
89	
90	3. Choose **Restore**.
91	
92	</Steps>
93	
94	<Shot
95	  name="15d-restore-graphic-version-sheet.sheet"
96	  alt="The Restore Graphic Version sheet. A paragraph explains that it puts back the newest kept version, keeps the code it replaces, and is not an Undo step. Graphic: is a pop-up reading lower-third, with 1 version kept in small grey type under it. Bottom right are Cancel and a blue Restore."
97	/>
98	
99	There's no list of versions to pick from. The sheet always restores the newest.
100	
101	The code a restore replaces is kept in its turn, and it becomes the newest. So restoring again returns to where you were, and the sheet swaps between those two rather than stepping further back. An agent can ask for any kept version.
102	
103	Restoring isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. The item is dimmed when no version of any graphic is kept. For when a version is kept, see [Kept versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/#kept-versions).
104	
105	## Duplicate as New Graphic
106	
107	Clips that share a module all change when it does. This writes a copy of the module under a new name and switches the selected clips to it, so you can change one clip's look and leave the rest alone.
108	
109	<Steps>
110	
111	1. Select the clips to split off.
112	
113	2. In the **Source** section of the **Graphic** sub-tab, choose **Duplicate as New Graphic…**.
114	
115	3. Type a module name. The field suggests `<name>-copy`, or `<name>-copy-2` and so on when that's taken.
116	
117	4. Choose **Duplicate**.
118	
119	</Steps>
120	
121	Writing the copy can't be undone, but switching the clips can, as one step, **Duplicate Graphic**. Undo puts the clips back on the original and leaves the copy in the folder. Use [Delete Graphic](#delete-graphic) to remove it.
122	
123	The button is dimmed when the module file is missing. When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, **Source** doesn't offer it.
124	
125	## When Frame Job won't do it
126	
127	On success, a sheet closes without a message. When Frame Job can't do what you asked it beeps, shows the reason in the sheet in its own words, and the sheet stays open so you can change your choice or choose **Cancel**.
128	
129	| Item | The sheet says | What it means |
130	| --- | --- | --- |
131	| Rename | `graphic name "My Title" is not a module name…` | The name breaks the rule above. |
132	| Rename | `graphics/title.js already exists` | Another module has that name. |
133	| Rename | `The name "title" is already drawn by clip 4 on the timeline…` | Clips left behind by a deleted module still use that name. Delete those clips or switch them first. |
134	| Delete | `The graphic "title" is still drawn by clips 4 and 9 on the timeline and clip 12 in nest 7…` | The sheet names every clip that uses it. Delete them or switch them to another module first. |
135	| Restore | `…was changed outside Frame Job and no longer holds the revision in its name; it is not restored…` | The kept file doesn't match what Frame Job stored, so nothing is written. |
136	
137	**Duplicate as New Graphic…** reports the same two naming problems in an alert. Its clips stay as they were.
138	
139	## With an agent
140	
141	`rename_graphic`, `delete_graphic` and `restore_graphic` do what the sheets do, and answer in the same words when they can't. `restore_graphic` can name any kept version, not only the newest.
142	
143	An agent duplicates a graphic with `write_graphic` of the module's code under the new name, then `set_graphic`. `set_graphic` can also point clips at a module that already exists, which the inspector can't do. An agent can't rename a module while a nest is open either.
144	
145	See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/) and [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
146

1	---
2	title: "Show video inside a graphic"
3	description: "Use a graphic as a matte so your footage plays through the shape it draws, and animate that shape like any other graphic."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A graphic can't read a video's pixels, but it can shape one. Make the graphic's track a matte and the video behind it shows only where the graphic draws, or, inverted, only where it doesn't.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Track ▸ Matte"
13	  tools={['set_track']}
14	/>
15	
16	## Show video inside a graphic
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Put the video on a track, and the graphic on the track directly above it. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
21	
22	2. Line the graphic clip up with the stretch of video you want cut. Where the matte track has no clip, the video shows uncut.
23	
24	3. Select the graphic clip.
25	
26	4. Choose **Track ▸ Matte ▸ Alpha**.
27	
28	</Steps>
29	
30	The graphic itself is no longer drawn. What it shows now decides where the video can be seen. To go back, choose **Track ▸ Matte ▸ Off**.
31	
32	## Choose a mode
33	
34	| Mode | The video shows where the graphic is |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| **Alpha** | Opaque |
37	| **Inverted Alpha** | Transparent |
38	| **Luma** | Bright |
39	| **Inverted Luma** | Dark |
40	
41	**Off** makes it an ordinary track again.
42	
43	## Write a module for a matte
44	
45	A matte module is written and called exactly like any other, and the cut follows each frame as it animates. Fill the window in white so it works in every mode.
46	
47	This one opens a rounded window with a spring:
48	
49	```js
50	export const meta = { name: "Window", durationInFrames: 90 };
51	export const schema = { radius: { type: "number", default: 24, min: 0, max: 200 } };
52	
53	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
54	  const t = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 18 });
55	  const w = ctx.width * 0.6 * t;
56	  const h = ctx.height * 0.6 * t;
57	  return svg(ctx, `<rect x="${(ctx.width - w) / 2}" y="${(ctx.height - h) / 2}"
58	    width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${props.radius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`);
59	}
60	```
61	
62	Its **radius** property appears on the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/) as usual, and you can [animate it](/graphics/animate-properties/). See [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/).
63	
64	## What the clip's settings still do
65	
66	The graphic clip's position, scale, opacity, crop and actions still shape the window, so you can move or fade it with the same controls as any clip.
67	
68	Its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing. They're kept, and they apply again if the track stops being a matte.
69	
70	The video's own drop shadow follows the cut-out shape.
71	
72	## Good to know
73	
74	Only the track directly behind the matte is cut, so tracks further back and the canvas show through the hole. [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/) has the whole story, including what happens with two matte tracks in a row and how a matte looks on the timeline.
75	
76	## Related
77	
78	- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
79	- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
80	- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
81	- [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/)

1	---
2	title: "Graphics playback and memory"
3	description: "How Frame Job keeps heavy graphics playing smoothly: drawing ahead, kept frames, Background render, and the memory they're allowed to use."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A graphic is drawn from code, frame by frame, and a heavy one can take longer to draw than a frame lasts. Frame Job works around that by drawing ahead of the playhead and keeping what it has drawn. Nearly all of this is automatic, and the one thing you can set is [Background render](#background-render).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Playback"
12	  keys="⌘,"
13	/>
14	
15	## Drawing ahead while playing
16	
17	While a preview plays forward over a project with a graphic in it, on the timeline or in a nest, Frame Job draws upcoming frames on spare processor cores ahead of the playhead. It uses one fewer core than your Mac has active.
18	
19	It starts again from the new spot on play, on a seek, and on an edit while playing. It runs to the end of the timeline, or to the end of the in and out range while playback is looping inside it.
20	
21	It doesn't run while the preview is paused or playing in reverse. Background render covers paused.
22	
23	## Kept frames
24	
25	A window keeps the graphic frames it has drawn in memory while it's open, so a stretch you play again comes from memory rather than being drawn again.
26	
27	A frame is matched by what it draws, so changing a module or a property only redraws the frames that come out different. Frames go when the window closes or newer frames replace them. The least recently used go first, and frames Background render drew ahead give way last.
28	
29	## Background render
30	
31	When you leave Frame Job alone, the window you last played or moved the playhead in draws its graphics ahead of the paused playhead, so the next play is smooth from the start.
32	
33	| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
34	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
35	| **Background render** | Turns background drawing on or off. | On | |
36	| **Start after … seconds** | How long Frame Job must be left alone first. | 5 | 1 to 60 |
37	
38	Find them in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Playback**. They save the moment you change them, with no **Save** button, and they apply to every project. The ⓘ on the **Playback** heading explains them.
39	
40	Background render needs a paused window that draws a graphic. It draws from the playhead to the end of the timeline, or to the end of the in and out range while playback would loop inside it, and it ends early if the [memory budget](#the-memory-budget) runs out. After that it waits for your next activity and the same wait before it runs again.
41	
42	It keeps the processor busy while it runs, and it carries on while Frame Job is hidden or covered. It doesn't stop your Mac going to sleep. It only draws graphic frames, and it changes nothing in your project or your export.
43	
44	## Set how long it waits
45	
46	**Start after … seconds** takes a whole number from 1 to 60, typed or with the stepper. The field and the stepper are live only while **Background render** is ticked. A typed number outside the range beeps and the stored value comes back.
47	
48	## What stops Background render
49	
50	Any activity in Frame Job stops the pass at once, and it starts again after the same wait.
51	
52	| Stops it | Doesn't stop it |
53	| --- | --- |
54	| A key, including a modifier key on its own | Moving the pointer |
55	| A click, a drag, a scroll or a trackpad gesture | Working in another app |
56	| Any edit, in any window | An agent's read-only call, such as `get_project` |
57	| Play, pause or a seek, in any window | |
58	| An agent's call that edits a project or moves a playhead | |
59	
60	It never runs while any window is playing.
61	
62	## The memory budget
63	
64	The frames drawn ahead and the frames kept share one budget for all of Frame Job. It's sized to your Mac, with no fixed cap in gigabytes.
65	
66	| Memory on your Mac | Budget |
67	| --- | --- |
68	| Normal | A quarter of its physical memory, so 8 GB on a 32 GB Mac |
69	| Short | An eighth |
70	| Critically short | Nothing. No frames are held, and each graphic is drawn when it's needed. |
71	
72	The frames an [export](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/#parallel-rendering) draws ahead count too. Frames being drawn ahead come first, and kept frames give up whatever room those need.
73	
74	Each playing window or export also holds at most 1,024 pictures ahead, however much memory is free.
75	
76	## What Frame Job skips
77	
78	### Repeat frames
79	
80	When a frame's SVG is the same as one already drawn, such as during a hold or in a static graphic, Frame Job reuses that picture. Your module still runs for every frame. Only the drawing of its SVG into a picture is skipped.
81	
82	While an [action](/graphics/animate-properties/) moves a property, every frame comes out different, so a graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the length of the action.
83	
84	### The picture cache
85	
86	PNG and JPEG pictures a graphic draws are decoded once and cached, so graphics full of pictures draw faster. The result is identical to drawing the original.
87	
88	The cache is a sixteenth of the graphics budget, so it shrinks when memory is short. The least recently used go first.
89	
90	## Good to know
91	
92	Each frame has 250 ms to draw in the preview. Past that the frame draws the [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card). An export allows 2 s, so a frame that fails in the preview can still export. See [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/).
93	
94	Background render is a setting for a person. No agent tool reads or writes it.
95	
96	## Related
97	
98	- [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/)
99	- [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/)
100	- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
101

1	---
2	title: "Graphics in exports"
3	description: "What an export draws for each graphic, what stops an export when one is broken, and where a graphic's warnings show up."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	An export draws each graphic the way the preview does, so the file matches what you saw. A broken graphic never reaches the file: the export stops and tells you which one and why.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
12	  keys="⌘E"
13	  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
14	/>
15	
16	## What an export draws
17	
18	An export draws each graphic as its module stood when the export was queued, whatever you edit next. Editing a module while an export runs doesn't change that file, and a job waiting in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) draws the code it was queued with.
19	
20	So you can carry on working on a module while an export runs. To get your new code into a file, export again.
21	
22	## Parallel rendering
23	
24	An export draws its graphics ahead on worker threads, one fewer than your Mac's active cores, so a graphics-heavy export doesn't wait on one frame at a time. The file is the same as drawing them one at a time.
25	
26	It isn't used for an animated GIF or APNG, for a single frame, or for an audio-only export. Frames drawn ahead share the [memory budget](/graphics/playback-and-memory/#the-memory-budget) with the preview's.
27	
28	## When a graphic won't compile
29	
30	An export that would draw a graphic whose module is missing or doesn't compile isn't started, and any file already at that path is left alone. The message names each graphic and its first error:
31	
32	> The export was not started: the graphic "title" does not compile — …; the graphic "logo" has no module in graphics/. Fix the module and export again.
33	
34	The check covers every graphic clip in the export's range, and every graphic in each nest reached from those clips. That's the whole nest, not only the part the export plays, so a broken graphic elsewhere in a nest stops the export too.
35	
36	An audio-only export isn't checked, because it draws no pictures.
37	
38	A job in the Export Queue reports this in its row when its turn comes, and it keeps the code it was queued with. Fix the module and export again.
39	
40	## When a graphic fails partway
41	
42	Compiling is the only check made before an export starts. A graphic that throws at frame 900 is found at frame 900. A graphic that fails partway through stops the export at that frame, and no file is left behind:
43	
44	> The export was stopped at frame 900 of the graphic "title": … No file was written.
45	
46	The frame number is the graphic's own, counted from its first frame. A frame fails when your code throws, when it takes more than 2 s to draw, or when its picture can't be made.
47	
48	To find a failure before a long export, play the graphic through in the preview and watch for the [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card). A frame has only 250 ms there, so the preview is the stricter of the two. A frame that takes between 250 ms and 2 s shows the card in the preview and exports normally.
49	
50	## Warnings in a finished export
51	
52	Warnings a graphic gives while drawing don't stop the export. Frame Job reports each distinct one when the file is done, with the graphic's name and the first frame it happened on.
53	
54	- The Exporting sheet's finish line adds a count, such as "1 graphic warning (hover for details)". Rest the pointer on the line to see each warning.
55	- An [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) row adds the count too, and its tooltip lists them.
56	
57	Each one reads like `"title" at frame 12: message`. A warning given on every frame counts once, and an export reports up to 64 distinct warnings.
58	
59	## The frozen clock
60	
61	The clock inside a graphic is frozen, so nothing depends on when it's drawn and an export matches the preview. `Date.now()` is always `946684800000`, and `new Date()` is always 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z.
62	
63	A graphic can't show today's date on its own, so give it the date through a [property](/graphics/properties/). A date you write out in the code, such as `new Date("2026-03-01")`, works as usual. The rest of the sandbox is on [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
64	
65	## Good to know
66	
67	**Save Frame** has no such stop. A graphic that fails draws its error card, and the card is what's saved. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
68	
69	## With an agent
70	
71	`export` answers straight away with a broken graphic's reason, before anything is queued. A failure while writing comes back from `export_status` as a failed job, naming the graphic and the frame, and a finished job lists the graphic warnings. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
72	
73	## Related
74	
75	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
76	- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
77	- [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/)
78	- [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/)

121	        let errors = diagnostics.filter { $0.level == "error" }.count
122	        let warnings = diagnostics.count - errors + folder.count
123	        return InspectorSection(
124	            id: "graphic.source", title: "Source",
125	            summary: {
126	                errors > 0 ? (errors == 1 ? "1 error" : "\(errors) errors")
127	                    : warnings > 0 ? (warnings == 1 ? "1 warning" : "\(warnings) warnings")
128	                    : metaName()
129	            },
130	            defaultExpanded: false,
131	            rows: rows)
132	    }

134	    /// Opens the shared module's file in the app the system gives `.js`.
135	    func openFile() {
136	        guard let url = shared()?.file?.url else { return NSSound.beep() }
137	        NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)
138	    }

140	    /// The module's compile, and `clip`'s first frame drawn and rasterized at
141	    /// the clip's own size — through the memo, and never recomputed while a
142	    /// live gesture runs.
143	    func report(
144	        for clip: ClipSnapshot, _ shared: Shared, libraryVersion: String
145	    ) -> GraphicClipReport {
146	        let module: GraphicModule, revision: String
147	        switch shared.entry {
148	        case nil:
149	            return GraphicClipReport(
150	                compile: [GraphicDiagnostic.noModule(shared.name)],
151	                render: [], frame: nil)
152	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _)?:
153	            return GraphicClipReport(compile: diagnostics, render: [], frame: nil)
154	        case .compiled(let compiled, let hash, _, _)?:
155	            module = compiled
156	            revision = hash
157	        }
158	        guard let graphic = clip.graphic, let document = binding.document else { return .empty }
159	        if document.isLiveEditing { return lastReports[clip.id] ?? .empty }
160	        guard let set = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey),
161	              let source = layerSource(of: clip),
162	              case .graphic(_, let hash, let frame, let propsJSON, let ctxJSON) = source
163	        else { return .empty }
164	        let key = [
165	            shared.name, revision, libraryVersion, hash, "\(graphic.width)×\(graphic.height)",
166	        ].joined(separator: "|")
167	        if let hit = reportMemo[key] {
168	            lastReports[clip.id] = hit
169	            return hit
170	        }
171	        var render: [GraphicDiagnostic] = []
172	        do {
173	            let drawn = try module.svg(
174	                frame: frame, propsJSON: propsJSON, ctxJSON: ctxJSON,
175	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.previewBudgetMs)
176	            render += drawn.warnings
177	            do {
178	                let raster = try set.library.rasterize(
179	                    drawn.svg, width: graphic.width, height: graphic.height)
180	                render += raster.warnings
181	            } catch {
182	                render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
183	            }
184	        } catch {
185	            render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
186	        }
187	        let report = GraphicClipReport(
188	            compile: module.compileWarnings, render: render, frame: frame)
189	        if reportMemo.count >= 64 { reportMemo.removeAll() }
190	        reportMemo[key] = report
191	        lastReports[clip.id] = report
192	        return report
193	    }
194	
195	    /// `clip`'s layer source in the recipe at its start, through
196	    /// `layerMemo`: `recipe(at:)` is asked only on a miss, and the memo is
197	    /// emptied when the binding's project is another handle.
198	    func layerSource(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> RecipeSourceRef? {
199	        guard let project = binding.project else { return nil }
200	        if project !== layerProject {
201	            layerMemo = [:]
202	            layerProject = project
203	        }
204	        if let hit = layerMemo[clip.id] { return hit }
205	        guard let layer = project.recipe(at: clip.start)?.layers
206	            .first(where: { $0.clip == clip.id })
207	        else { return nil }
208	        layerMemo[clip.id] = layer.source
209	        return layer.source
210	    }

212	    /// Copies the module's file under a new name the person types, then
213	    /// repoints the selected clips at it with `set_graphic {name}` — the
214	    /// copy is not undoable (G-3), the repoint is one step. The MCP mirror is
215	    /// `write_graphic` of the source under the new name, then `set_graphic`.
216	    func duplicateAsNewGraphic(_ file: GraphicModuleFile, schema: [String: Any]?) {
217	        guard let store = binding.document?.graphicStore else { return NSSound.beep() }
218	        let suggestion = store.uniqueModuleName(file.name + "-copy")
219	        let alert = NSAlert()
220	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
221	        alert.messageText = "Duplicate \(file.name).js as a new graphic"
222	        alert.informativeText =
223	            "The copy is written into the package's graphics/ folder and the selected clips "
224	            + "are drawn by it. Writing the file cannot be undone; switching the clips can."
225	        let field = NSTextField(string: suggestion)
226	        field.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: 24)
227	        field.placeholderString = "Module name"
228	        alert.accessoryView = field
229	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Duplicate")
230	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
231	        alert.window.initialFirstResponder = field
232	        guard alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return }
233	        let name = field.stringValue.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
234	        func refuse(_ sentence: String) {
235	            NSAlert(error: NSError(
236	                domain: "FrameJob", code: 1, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: sentence]))
237	                .runModal()
238	        }
239	        guard GraphicStore.isModuleName(name) else { return refuse(GraphicStore.nameSentence(name)) }
240	        guard !store.holdsModule(named: name) else {
241	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js already exists")
242	        }
243	        do {
244	            try store.write(name: name, source: String(decoding: file.bytes, as: UTF8.self))
245	        } catch {
246	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js could not be written: \(error.localizedDescription)")
247	        }
248	        store.rescan()
249	        let clips = binding.graphicClips.map(\.id)
250	        binding.apply(
251	            "Duplicate Graphic",
252	            clips.isEmpty ? [] : [.setGraphicRaw(clips: clips, patch: ["name": name], schema: schema)])
253	    }
254	}

1	// app/Sources/GraphicStore+Files.swift — the store's own writes into
2	// `graphics/`: the free-name rule and the module write (road map 10 §5f).
3	//
4	// **A name is taken when the scan holds it OR its file is on disk**, so a
5	// module written from the shell a moment before is never overwritten by a
6	// stale scan (#75). **A file lands through `land(at:writing:)`**: a
7	// `.partial` beside it, then moved into place, and on any failure the
8	// `.partial` is removed. `removeScratchRoot()` removes the untitled root
9	// (spec §11 G-19 (d)).
10	//
11	// **`removeModule` and `moveModule` are the app's delete and rename** (spec
12	// §11 G-27, G-28), each inside `onQueue` so no pass runs between their
13	// steps: the first keeps the file's bytes and then removes it, the second
14	// moves the file, journals the pair and moves its history, and a throw
15	// part-way leaves the file, the history and the journal where they were.
16	// Neither rescans.
17	
18	import CryptoKit
19	import Foundation
20	
21	extension GraphicStore {
22	    /// `base` when no module of that name is held, else `base-2`,
23	    /// `base-3`, … — `base` cut to 60 scalars first, so a suffix fits.
24	    func uniqueModuleName(_ base: String) -> String {
25	        let root = String(String.UnicodeScalarView(base.unicodeScalars.prefix(60)))
26	        guard holdsModule(named: root) else { return root }
27	        var n = 2
28	        while holdsModule(named: "\(root)-\(n)") { n += 1 }
29	        return "\(root)-\(n)"
30	    }
31	
32	    /// True when the scan holds `name` or `<name>.js` is on disk.
33	    func holdsModule(named name: String) -> Bool {
34	        scan.modules[name] != nil
35	            || FileManager.default.fileExists(
36	                atPath: folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name + ".js").path)
37	    }
38	
39	    /// The app's own write: `<name>.js.partial`, then moved into place, so
40	    /// a reader never sees half a module.
41	    func write(name: String, source: String) throws {
42	        try write(name: name, bytes: Data(source.utf8))
43	    }
44	
45	    /// `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are — a kept revision put
46	    /// back byte for byte.
47	    func write(name: String, bytes: Data) throws {
48	        guard Self.isModuleName(name) else { throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.nameSentence(name)) }
49	        try ensureFolder()
50	        writeManual()
51	        _ = try Self.land(at: folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name + ".js")) {
52	            try bytes.write(to: $0)
53	        }
54	    }
55	
56	    /// Main. Keeps `<name>.js`'s bytes as its newest kept text, then
57	    /// removes the file; the kept revision. The caller rescans. A file whose
58	    /// text could not be kept is not removed (G-27 (c)).
59	    func removeModule(named name: String) throws -> String {
60	        try onQueue {
61	            let url = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name + ".js")
62	            let bytes = try Data(contentsOf: url)
63	            let revision = Self.hex(SHA256.hash(data: bytes))
64	            Self.keep(bytes, named: name, in: folderURL)
65	            guard kept(named: name).first?.revision == revision else {
66	                throw ReelCoreError(
67	                    message: "its text could not be kept in graphics/"
68	                        + "\(Self.historyFolderName)/\(name)/")
69	            }
70	            do {
71	                try FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url)
72	            } catch {
73	                Self.dropKept(revision: revision, named: name, in: folderURL)
74	                throw error
75	            }
76	            return revision
77	        }
78	    }
79	
80	    /// Main. Moves `<from>.js` to `<to>.js`, journals the pair, and moves
81	    /// its history with it; a throw leaves the file, the history and the
82	    /// journal where they were. **A rename that could not be journalled is
83	    /// refused** (G-28 (d)): the pair is written, and read back, before the
84	    /// history is folded — a fold cannot be undone — so no rename succeeds
85	    /// that Undo could not repair. When the history then fails to move, the
86	    /// journal is put back as it was read (its bytes, or no file): a
87	    /// refused rename journals no pair, and an earlier pair of the same two
88	    /// names is still there for Undo. A crash between the three steps is
89	    /// G-28 (f)'s limit. The caller checks the names and rescans.
90	    func moveModule(from: String, to: String) throws {
91	        try onQueue {
92	            let files = FileManager.default
93	            let source = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(from + ".js")
94	            let target = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(to + ".js")
95	            let journalled = Self.renameJournalBytes(in: folderURL)
96	            try files.moveItem(at: source, to: target)
97	            Self.recordRename(from, to, in: folderURL)
98	            guard let newest = renamePairs().first, newest == (from, to) else {
99	                try? files.moveItem(at: target, to: source)
100	                throw ReelCoreError(
101	                    message: "its rename could not be journalled in graphics/"
102	                        + "\(Self.historyFolderName)/\(Self.renameJournalName)")
103	            }
104	            do {
105	                try Self.moveHistory(from: from, to: to, in: folderURL)
106	            } catch {
107	                try? files.moveItem(at: target, to: source)
108	                Self.putBackRenameJournal(journalled, in: folderURL)
109	                throw error
110	            }
111	        }
112	    }
113	
114	    /// The sentence for a module the folder does not hold, naming what it does.
115	    func noModuleSentence(_ name: String) -> String {
116	        let held = scan.modules.keys.sorted()
117	        let listed = held.isEmpty ? "nothing" : held.joined(separator: ", ")
118	        return "No module named \"\(name)\" in graphics/ — the folder holds: \(listed)"
119	    }
120	
121	    /// Writes `<target>.partial` through `write` (any stale one removed
122	    /// first), then replaces `target` with it, or moves it into place when
123	    /// there is none. On any throw the partial is removed and the error
124	    /// rethrown. Whether it replaced.
125	    static func land(at target: URL, writing write: (URL) throws -> Void) throws -> Bool {
126	        let files = FileManager.default
127	        let partial = target.deletingLastPathComponent()
128	            .appendingPathComponent(target.lastPathComponent + ".partial")
129	        try? files.removeItem(at: partial)
130	        do {
131	            try write(partial)
132	            if files.fileExists(atPath: target.path) {
133	                _ = try files.replaceItemAt(target, withItemAt: partial)
134	                return true
135	            }
136	            try files.moveItem(at: partial, to: target)
137	            return false
138	        } catch {
139	            try? files.removeItem(at: partial)
140	            throw error
141	        }
142	    }
143	
144	    /// Main, after `stop()`: the untitled root is removed; a package's
145	    /// `graphics/` is never touched (G-14, G-19 (d)).
146	    func removeScratchRoot() {
147	        guard package == nil else { return }
148	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: folderURL)
149	    }
150	}

1	// app/Sources/GraphicStore+Manual.swift — the graphics reference written
2	// into a package's `graphics/` (road map 10's G4a): `API.md` and `API.d.ts`,
3	// copies of the app's bundled `GraphicsAPI.md` and `GraphicsAPI.d.ts`, so an
4	// agent or a person editing the folder has the API beside the modules.
5	//
6	// **The manual is never a reason to create `graphics/`** (spec §11 G-14):
7	// `writeManual()` writes nothing unless the folder already exists, and
8	// `holdsContent` does not count the manual, so an untitled root holding only
9	// the manual is not carried by a save.
10	
11	import Foundation
12	
13	extension GraphicStore {
14	    /// What the manual is called inside `graphics/`.
15	    static let manualNames = ["API.md", "API.d.ts"]
16	    /// What it is called in the app's Resources, in `manualNames`' order.
17	    static let bundledManualNames = ["GraphicsAPI.md", "GraphicsAPI.d.ts"]
18	
19	    /// The directory holding `Fonts/`, which holds the manual too. The
20	    /// harness copies the manual there; the probes copy none, so for them
21	    /// `writeManual()` is a no-op.
22	    static func manualDirectory(besideFonts fonts: URL) -> URL {
23	        fonts.deletingLastPathComponent()
24	    }
25	
26	    var manualDirectory: URL { Self.manualDirectory(besideFonts: bundledFonts) }
27	
28	    /// The app bundle's own `GraphicsAPI.md`, no document involved:
29	    /// `graphic_reference` answers it and Help ▸ Graphics Reference opens it.
30	    static var bundledReferenceURL: URL {
31	        manualDirectory(besideFonts: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory)
32	            .appendingPathComponent(bundledManualNames[0])
33	    }
34	
35	    /// Main. Nothing unless `folderURL` exists; each file written
36	    /// (`.atomic`) only when its bytes differ from the bundled one; a
37	    /// bundled file that is absent is skipped silently.
38	    func writeManual() {
39	        let files = FileManager.default
40	        guard files.fileExists(atPath: folderURL.path) else { return }
41	        for (bundled, name) in zip(Self.bundledManualNames, Self.manualNames) {
42	            guard let bytes = try? Data(
43	                contentsOf: manualDirectory.appendingPathComponent(bundled))
44	            else { continue }
45	            let target = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name)
46	            if let current = try? Data(contentsOf: target), current == bytes { continue }
47	            try? bytes.write(to: target, options: .atomic)
48	        }
49	    }
50	
51	    /// True when `folder` holds ANY entry, file or directory, that is
52	    /// neither hidden, one of `manualNames`, nor a `.partial`. A `fonts/` or
53	    /// `assets/` subfolder counts; `listing(_:)`'s regular-files rule is not
54	    /// this.
55	    static func holdsContent(_ folder: URL) -> Bool {
56	        let entries = (try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(
57	            at: folder, includingPropertiesForKeys: nil,
58	            options: [.skipsHiddenFiles])) ?? []
59	        return entries.contains {
60	            !manualNames.contains($0.lastPathComponent) && $0.pathExtension != "partial"
61	        }
62	    }
63	}

2	// `graphics/` folder: a module file, a font or asset file, and one pass's
3	// scan (road map 10 §5f, G3a). A pure move out of `GraphicStore.swift`.

5	import CryptoKit
6	import Foundation
7	
8	/// One module file: its name (the file's stem), its bytes and its revision,
9	/// the SHA-256 of the bytes as 64 lowercase hex digits (G-13).
10	struct GraphicModuleFile: Equatable {
11	    let name: String, url: URL, bytes: Data, revision: String
12	}
13

16	    let name: String, url: URL, bytes: Data
17	}
18

21	    let modules: [String: GraphicModuleFile]
22	    let fonts: [GraphicFile], assets: [GraphicFile]
23	    /// The SHA-256 over the fonts then the assets, each name then bytes, in
24	    /// name order. The empty set hashes nothing.

27	    /// sentence.

29	
30	    static let empty = GraphicScan.empty(warnings: [])
31	
32	    /// Nothing found, with `warnings`: a package whose source did not arm.

35	            modules: [:], fonts: [], assets: [],
36	            libraryVersion: GraphicStore.hex(SHA256().finalize()), warnings: warnings)
37	    }

1	// app/Sources/GraphicRegistry.swift — the compiled graphics each document
2	// draws with (road map 10 §5f's registry paragraph, G3b): a `RecipeSource`
3	// key → one immutable `GraphicSet`, the library and every module of that
4	// document's `graphics/` compiled against it.
5	//
6	// **Preview follows the newest revision** (G-13): the document installs its
7	// set when its store starts and swaps a NEW set in on every
8	// `.graphicsDidChange` (`ProjectDocument+Graphics.swift`). A font or asset
9	// change builds a new library and recompiles every module against it — a
10	// library is frozen by its first compile — and anything else recompiles only
11	// the named modules against the existing library. Nothing here calls
12	// `store.rescan()`: `drain()` is not re-entrant (road map 10 §10.6 G3a).
13	//
14	// **Threading.** `install`, `update`, `remove` and `entry` are main-only,
15	// because the store's scan is. `resolve`, `snapshot` and the pin's five
16	// calls are any-thread — the compositor's render queue and a `render_frame`
17	// generator thread — and the lock covers only the two maps; a module draws
18	// on a thread that did not compile it (the engine keeps per-thread
19	// runtimes, G1c).
20	//
21	// **An offline key** — the one `Exporter.renderFrame` or an export mints —
22	// draws with the set its caller PINNED on it (G-13, G3c): the document's
23	// set as it stood when the export or the frame was asked for, retained for
24	// the key's life however the document's own set changes. A key with no
25	// set and no pin resolves nil and the layer draws the slate. A pin also
26	// holds what the key's graphics REPORTED — the first failure in a slot of
27	// its own, then up to 64 warnings distinct by graphic and messages, the
28	// frame aside, so one graphic warning every frame keeps one (G-24 (c)) — for
29	// `render_frame`'s reply, the export's abort and its `graphicWarnings`.
30	
31	import Foundation
32	
33	/// One document's compiled graphics at one instant. Immutable: a change
34	/// makes a new one, so a frame in flight keeps a coherent set.
35	final class GraphicSet {
36	    let library: GraphicLibrary
37	    /// The store's `GraphicScan.libraryVersion` the library was built from —
38	    /// part of the texture key, so a font change never serves an old raster.
39	    let libraryVersion: String
40	    let modules: [String: GraphicRegistry.Entry]
41	    /// The library could not be built, so `library` is an empty stand-in:
42	    /// no module may be compiled against it, and `update` rebuilds instead.
43	    let libraryFailed: Bool
44	
45	    init(
46	        library: GraphicLibrary, libraryVersion: String, modules: [String: GraphicRegistry.Entry],
47	        libraryFailed: Bool = false
48	    ) {
49	        self.library = library
50	        self.libraryVersion = libraryVersion
51	        self.modules = modules
52	        self.libraryFailed = libraryFailed
53	    }
54	}
55	
56	/// What one graphic reported while an offline key drew it: a failure (the
57	/// error card was drawn) or a warning, with the graphic's own frame — nil
58	/// when the module did not compile.
59	struct GraphicReport: Equatable {
60	    let name: String
61	    let frame: Int?
62	    let failed: Bool
63	    let diagnostics: [GraphicDiagnostic]
64	}
65	
66	final class GraphicRegistry {
67	    static let shared = GraphicRegistry()
68	
69	    /// The engine's budgets, in milliseconds: a compile, one preview frame,
70	    /// and one frame of an export or a `render_frame`.
71	    static let compileBudgetMs = 250, previewBudgetMs = 250, offlineBudgetMs = 2000
72	
73	    /// One module as compiled against a set's library: the module with its
74	    /// file's revision and its `describe` parsed, or why it did not compile.
75	    enum Entry {
76	        case compiled(GraphicModule, revision: String, meta: [String: Any], schema: [String: Any])
77	        case failed([GraphicDiagnostic], revision: String)
78	    }
79	
80	    /// An offline key's pinned set and what its graphics reported. The
81	    /// FIRST failure owns `failure` for the pin's life, so a graphic that
82	    /// warns on every frame can fill `warnings` and never hide it.
83	    private struct Pin {
84	        let set: GraphicSet
85	        var failure: GraphicReport?
86	        var warnings: [GraphicReport]
87	    }
88	
89	    /// Warnings a pin keeps; a later distinct one is dropped.
90	    static let warningLimit = 64
91	
92	    private let lock = NSLock()
93	    private var sets: [Int: GraphicSet] = [:]
94	    private var pins: [Int: Pin] = [:]
95	
96	    private init() {}
97	
98	    /// Compiles every module the store's scan holds against a NEW library
99	    /// and publishes the set under `key`. Main.
100	    func install(_ store: GraphicStore, for key: Int) {
101	        let scan = store.scan
102	        let set: GraphicSet
103	        do {
104	            let library = try store.makeLibrary()
105	            set = GraphicSet(
106	                library: library, libraryVersion: scan.libraryVersion,
107	                modules: scan.modules.mapValues { Self.compile($0, library: library) })
108	        } catch {
109	            // The library could not be built (a font the engine refused):
110	            // every module fails with that sentence and draws the slate.
111	            let reason = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
112	            set = GraphicSet(
113	                library: GraphicLibrary(), libraryVersion: scan.libraryVersion,
114	                modules: scan.modules.mapValues { .failed(reason, revision: $0.revision) },
115	                libraryFailed: true)
116	        }
117	        publish(set, for: key)
118	    }
119	
120	    /// Answers one `.graphicsDidChange`. `library` true is a font or asset
121	    /// change: a new library and every module recompiled. Otherwise only
122	    /// `names` are recompiled, against the EXISTING library — a frozen
123	    /// library refuses adds, not compiles — and a name the scan no longer
124	    /// holds is dropped. A set whose library failed is rebuilt whole, so no
125	    /// module compiles against its empty stand-in. Always a new set. Main.
126	    func update(_ store: GraphicStore, for key: Int, names: [String], library: Bool) {
127	        lock.lock()
128	        let current = sets[key]
129	        lock.unlock()
130	        guard let current = current, !library, !current.libraryFailed else {
131	            install(store, for: key)
132	            return
133	        }
134	        let scan = store.scan
135	        var modules = current.modules
136	        for name in names {
137	            if let file = scan.modules[name] {
138	                modules[name] = Self.compile(file, library: current.library)
139	            } else {
140	                modules.removeValue(forKey: name)
141	            }
142	        }
143	        publish(
144	            GraphicSet(
145	                library: current.library, libraryVersion: current.libraryVersion,
146	                modules: modules),
147	            for: key)
148	    }
149	
150	    /// Drops a document's set, when its store stops. Main.
151	    func remove(_ key: Int) {
152	        lock.lock()
153	        defer { lock.unlock() }
154	        sets.removeValue(forKey: key)
155	    }
156	
157	    /// The module `name` as the document keyed `key` has it compiled — the
158	    /// op tools' read of `meta` and `schema`. Main.
159	    func entry(named name: String, for key: Int) -> Entry? {
160	        lock.lock()
161	        defer { lock.unlock() }
162	        return sets[key]?.modules[name]
163	    }
164	
165	    /// The set a document keyed `key` draws with right now — what an export
166	    /// or a `render_frame` pins. Any thread.
167	    func snapshot(for key: Int) -> GraphicSet? {
168	        lock.lock()
169	        defer { lock.unlock() }
170	        return sets[key]
171	    }
172	
173	    /// Opens `key`'s pin on `set`: an offline key draws with it until
174	    /// `unpin`, and records its reports. Any thread.
175	    func pin(_ set: GraphicSet, for key: Int) {
176	        lock.lock()
177	        defer { lock.unlock() }
178	        pins[key] = Pin(set: set, failure: nil, warnings: [])
179	    }
180	
181	    /// Drops `key`'s pin and its reports; a no-op for a key never pinned.
182	    /// Any thread.
183	    func unpin(_ key: Int) {
184	        lock.lock()
185	        defer { lock.unlock() }
186	        pins.removeValue(forKey: key)
187	    }
188	
189	    /// Keeps `report` against a pinned key; a no-op for any other key. A
190	    /// failure fills the failure slot if it is empty and is dropped
191	    /// otherwise; a warning is appended unless the same one (`sameWarning`)
192	    /// is held or `warningLimit` are. Any thread.
193	    func record(_ report: GraphicReport, for key: Int) {
194	        lock.lock()
195	        defer { lock.unlock() }
196	        guard var pin = pins[key] else { return }
197	        if report.failed {
198	            guard pin.failure == nil else { return }
199	            pin.failure = report
200	        } else {
201	            guard pin.warnings.count < Self.warningLimit,
202	                !pin.warnings.contains(where: { Self.sameWarning($0, report) })
203	            else { return }
204	            pin.warnings.append(report)
205	        }
206	        pins[key] = pin
207	    }
208	
209	    /// Everything `key`'s pin holds: the failure first, then the warnings in
210	    /// the order they arrived. Any thread.
211	    func reports(for key: Int) -> [GraphicReport] {
212	        lock.lock()
213	        defer { lock.unlock() }
214	        guard let pin = pins[key] else { return [] }
215	        return (pin.failure.map { [$0] } ?? []) + pin.warnings
216	    }
217	
218	    /// One graphic's same warning at another frame: the name and every
219	    /// diagnostic's located message equal, the frame aside (G-24 (c)).
220	    static func sameWarning(_ a: GraphicReport, _ b: GraphicReport) -> Bool {
221	        a.name == b.name && a.diagnostics.map(\.located) == b.diagnostics.map(\.located)
222	    }
223	
224	    /// The pin's failure slot — the first failure it recorded. Any thread.
225	    func failure(for key: Int) -> GraphicReport? {
226	        lock.lock()
227	        defer { lock.unlock() }
228	        return pins[key]?.failure
229	    }
230	
231	    /// The set a recipe under `key` draws with, and the per-frame budget:
232	    /// a document's own key answers its set at the preview budget; a
233	    /// pinned offline key answers its pinned set at the offline budget;
234	    /// anything else is nil. Any thread.
235	    func resolve(_ key: Int) -> (set: GraphicSet, budgetMs: Int)? {
236	        lock.lock()
237	        defer { lock.unlock() }
238	        if let own = sets[key] { return (own, Self.previewBudgetMs) }
239	        if let pinned = pins[key] { return (pinned.set, Self.offlineBudgetMs) }
240	        return nil
241	    }
242	
243	    private func publish(_ set: GraphicSet, for key: Int) {
244	        lock.lock()
245	        defer { lock.unlock() }
246	        sets[key] = set
247	    }
248	
249	    /// One module file compiled against `library`, its `describe` parsed.
250	    static func compile(_ file: GraphicModuleFile, library: GraphicLibrary) -> Entry {
251	        let source = String(decoding: file.bytes, as: UTF8.self)
252	        do {
253	            let module = try GraphicModule.compile(
254	                library: library, name: file.name, source: source, budgetMs: compileBudgetMs)
255	            let described = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(
256	                with: Data(module.describeJSON().utf8))) as? [String: Any]
257	            return .compiled(
258	                module, revision: file.revision,
259	                meta: described?["meta"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:],
260	                schema: described?["schema"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:])
261	        } catch {
262	            return .failed(GraphicDiagnostic.of(error), revision: file.revision)
263	        }
264	    }
265	}
266	
267	extension GraphicModule {
268	    /// `describeJSON()`'s `warnings` — what the module's top level warned as
269	    /// it loaded (G-21 (b), G-24 (a)) — decoded; `[]` when absent or
270	    /// unreadable. Main or any thread.
271	    var compileWarnings: [GraphicDiagnostic] {
272	        struct Described: Decodable { let warnings: [GraphicDiagnostic]? }
273	        let described = try? JSONDecoder().decode(Described.self, from: Data(describeJSON().utf8))
274	        return described?.warnings ?? []
275	    }
276	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

140	    /// The module's compile, and `clip`'s first frame drawn and rasterized at
141	    /// the clip's own size — through the memo, and never recomputed while a
142	    /// live gesture runs.
143	    func report(
144	        for clip: ClipSnapshot, _ shared: Shared, libraryVersion: String
145	    ) -> GraphicClipReport {
146	        let module: GraphicModule, revision: String
147	        switch shared.entry {
148	        case nil:
149	            return GraphicClipReport(
150	                compile: [GraphicDiagnostic.noModule(shared.name)],
151	                render: [], frame: nil)
152	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _)?:
153	            return GraphicClipReport(compile: diagnostics, render: [], frame: nil)
154	        case .compiled(let compiled, let hash, _, _)?:
155	            module = compiled
156	            revision = hash
157	        }
158	        guard let graphic = clip.graphic, let document = binding.document else { return .empty }
159	        if document.isLiveEditing { return lastReports[clip.id] ?? .empty }
160	        guard let set = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey),
161	              let source = layerSource(of: clip),
162	              case .graphic(_, let hash, let frame, let propsJSON, let ctxJSON) = source
163	        else { return .empty }
164	        let key = [
165	            shared.name, revision, libraryVersion, hash, "\(graphic.width)×\(graphic.height)",
166	        ].joined(separator: "|")
167	        if let hit = reportMemo[key] {
168	            lastReports[clip.id] = hit
169	            return hit
170	        }
171	        var render: [GraphicDiagnostic] = []
172	        do {
173	            let drawn = try module.svg(
174	                frame: frame, propsJSON: propsJSON, ctxJSON: ctxJSON,
175	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.previewBudgetMs)
176	            render += drawn.warnings
177	            do {
178	                let raster = try set.library.rasterize(
179	                    drawn.svg, width: graphic.width, height: graphic.height)
180	                render += raster.warnings
181	            } catch {
182	                render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
183	            }
184	        } catch {
185	            render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
186	        }
187	        let report = GraphicClipReport(
188	            compile: module.compileWarnings, render: render, frame: frame)
189	        if reportMemo.count >= 64 { reportMemo.removeAll() }
190	        reportMemo[key] = report
191	        lastReports[clip.id] = report
192	        return report
193	    }
194	
195	    /// `clip`'s layer source in the recipe at its start, through
196	    /// `layerMemo`: `recipe(at:)` is asked only on a miss, and the memo is
197	    /// emptied when the binding's project is another handle.
198	    func layerSource(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> RecipeSourceRef? {
199	        guard let project = binding.project else { return nil }
200	        if project !== layerProject {
201	            layerMemo = [:]
202	            layerProject = project
203	        }
204	        if let hit = layerMemo[clip.id] { return hit }
205	        guard let layer = project.recipe(at: clip.start)?.layers
206	            .first(where: { $0.clip == clip.id })
207	        else { return nil }
208	        layerMemo[clip.id] = layer.source
209	        return layer.source
210	    }

212	    /// Copies the module's file under a new name the person types, then
213	    /// repoints the selected clips at it with `set_graphic {name}` — the
214	    /// copy is not undoable (G-3), the repoint is one step. The MCP mirror is
215	    /// `write_graphic` of the source under the new name, then `set_graphic`.
216	    func duplicateAsNewGraphic(_ file: GraphicModuleFile, schema: [String: Any]?) {
217	        guard let store = binding.document?.graphicStore else { return NSSound.beep() }
218	        let suggestion = store.uniqueModuleName(file.name + "-copy")
219	        let alert = NSAlert()
220	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
221	        alert.messageText = "Duplicate \(file.name).js as a new graphic"
222	        alert.informativeText =
223	            "The copy is written into the package's graphics/ folder and the selected clips "
224	            + "are drawn by it. Writing the file cannot be undone; switching the clips can."
225	        let field = NSTextField(string: suggestion)
226	        field.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: 24)
227	        field.placeholderString = "Module name"
228	        alert.accessoryView = field
229	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Duplicate")
230	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
231	        alert.window.initialFirstResponder = field
232	        guard alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return }
233	        let name = field.stringValue.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
234	        func refuse(_ sentence: String) {
235	            NSAlert(error: NSError(
236	                domain: "FrameJob", code: 1, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: sentence]))
237	                .runModal()
238	        }
239	        guard GraphicStore.isModuleName(name) else { return refuse(GraphicStore.nameSentence(name)) }
240	        guard !store.holdsModule(named: name) else {
241	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js already exists")
242	        }
243	        do {
244	            try store.write(name: name, source: String(decoding: file.bytes, as: UTF8.self))
245	        } catch {
246	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js could not be written: \(error.localizedDescription)")
247	        }
248	        store.rescan()
249	        let clips = binding.graphicClips.map(\.id)
250	        binding.apply(
251	            "Duplicate Graphic",
252	            clips.isEmpty ? [] : [.setGraphicRaw(clips: clips, patch: ["name": name], schema: schema)])
253	    }
254	}

1	// app/Sources/GraphicStore+Files.swift — the store's own writes into
2	// `graphics/`: the free-name rule and the module write (road map 10 §5f).
3	//
4	// **A name is taken when the scan holds it OR its file is on disk**, so a
5	// module written from the shell a moment before is never overwritten by a
6	// stale scan (#75). **A file lands through `land(at:writing:)`**: a
7	// `.partial` beside it, then moved into place, and on any failure the
8	// `.partial` is removed. `removeScratchRoot()` removes the untitled root
9	// (spec §11 G-19 (d)).
10	//
11	// **`removeModule` and `moveModule` are the app's delete and rename** (spec
12	// §11 G-27, G-28), each inside `onQueue` so no pass runs between their
13	// steps: the first keeps the file's bytes and then removes it, the second
14	// moves the file, journals the pair and moves its history, and a throw
15	// part-way leaves the file, the history and the journal where they were.
16	// Neither rescans.
17	
18	import CryptoKit
19	import Foundation
20	
21	extension GraphicStore {
22	    /// `base` when no module of that name is held, else `base-2`,
23	    /// `base-3`, … — `base` cut to 60 scalars first, so a suffix fits.
24	    func uniqueModuleName(_ base: String) -> String {
25	        let root = String(String.UnicodeScalarView(base.unicodeScalars.prefix(60)))
26	        guard holdsModule(named: root) else { return root }
27	        var n = 2
28	        while holdsModule(named: "\(root)-\(n)") { n += 1 }
29	        return "\(root)-\(n)"
30	    }
31	
32	    /// True when the scan holds `name` or `<name>.js` is on disk.
33	    func holdsModule(named name: String) -> Bool {
34	        scan.modules[name] != nil
35	            || FileManager.default.fileExists(
36	                atPath: folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name + ".js").path)
37	    }
38	
39	    /// The app's own write: `<name>.js.partial`, then moved into place, so
40	    /// a reader never sees half a module.
41	    func write(name: String, source: String) throws {
42	        try write(name: name, bytes: Data(source.utf8))
43	    }
44	
45	    /// `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are — a kept revision put
46	    /// back byte for byte.
47	    func write(name: String, bytes: Data) throws {
48	        guard Self.isModuleName(name) else { throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.nameSentence(name)) }
49	        try ensureFolder()
50	        writeManual()
51	        _ = try Self.land(at: folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name + ".js")) {
52	            try bytes.write(to: $0)
53	        }
54	    }
55	
56	    /// Main. Keeps `<name>.js`'s bytes as its newest kept text, then
57	    /// removes the file; the kept revision. The caller rescans. A file whose
58	    /// text could not be kept is not removed (G-27 (c)).
59	    func removeModule(named name: String) throws -> String {
60	        try onQueue {
61	            let url = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name + ".js")
62	            let bytes = try Data(contentsOf: url)
63	            let revision = Self.hex(SHA256.hash(data: bytes))
64	            Self.keep(bytes, named: name, in: folderURL)
65	            guard kept(named: name).first?.revision == revision else {
66	                throw ReelCoreError(
67	                    message: "its text could not be kept in graphics/"
68	                        + "\(Self.historyFolderName)/\(name)/")
69	            }
70	            do {
71	                try FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url)
72	            } catch {
73	                Self.dropKept(revision: revision, named: name, in: folderURL)
74	                throw error
75	            }
76	            return revision
77	        }
78	    }
79	
80	    /// Main. Moves `<from>.js` to `<to>.js`, journals the pair, and moves
81	    /// its history with it; a throw leaves the file, the history and the
82	    /// journal where they were. **A rename that could not be journalled is
83	    /// refused** (G-28 (d)): the pair is written, and read back, before the
84	    /// history is folded — a fold cannot be undone — so no rename succeeds
85	    /// that Undo could not repair. When the history then fails to move, the
86	    /// journal is put back as it was read (its bytes, or no file): a
87	    /// refused rename journals no pair, and an earlier pair of the same two
88	    /// names is still there for Undo. A crash between the three steps is
89	    /// G-28 (f)'s limit. The caller checks the names and rescans.
90	    func moveModule(from: String, to: String) throws {
91	        try onQueue {
92	            let files = FileManager.default
93	            let source = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(from + ".js")
94	            let target = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(to + ".js")
95	            let journalled = Self.renameJournalBytes(in: folderURL)
96	            try files.moveItem(at: source, to: target)
97	            Self.recordRename(from, to, in: folderURL)
98	            guard let newest = renamePairs().first, newest == (from, to) else {
99	                try? files.moveItem(at: target, to: source)
100	                throw ReelCoreError(
101	                    message: "its rename could not be journalled in graphics/"
102	                        + "\(Self.historyFolderName)/\(Self.renameJournalName)")
103	            }
104	            do {
105	                try Self.moveHistory(from: from, to: to, in: folderURL)
106	            } catch {
107	                try? files.moveItem(at: target, to: source)
108	                Self.putBackRenameJournal(journalled, in: folderURL)
109	                throw error
110	            }
111	        }
112	    }
113	
114	    /// The sentence for a module the folder does not hold, naming what it does.
115	    func noModuleSentence(_ name: String) -> String {
116	        let held = scan.modules.keys.sorted()
117	        let listed = held.isEmpty ? "nothing" : held.joined(separator: ", ")
118	        return "No module named \"\(name)\" in graphics/ — the folder holds: \(listed)"
119	    }
120	
121	    /// Writes `<target>.partial` through `write` (any stale one removed
122	    /// first), then replaces `target` with it, or moves it into place when
123	    /// there is none. On any throw the partial is removed and the error
124	    /// rethrown. Whether it replaced.
125	    static func land(at target: URL, writing write: (URL) throws -> Void) throws -> Bool {
126	        let files = FileManager.default
127	        let partial = target.deletingLastPathComponent()
128	            .appendingPathComponent(target.lastPathComponent + ".partial")
129	        try? files.removeItem(at: partial)
130	        do {
131	            try write(partial)
132	            if files.fileExists(atPath: target.path) {
133	                _ = try files.replaceItemAt(target, withItemAt: partial)
134	                return true
135	            }
136	            try files.moveItem(at: partial, to: target)
137	            return false
138	        } catch {
139	            try? files.removeItem(at: partial)
140	            throw error
141	        }
142	    }
143	
144	    /// Main, after `stop()`: the untitled root is removed; a package's
145	    /// `graphics/` is never touched (G-14, G-19 (d)).
146	    func removeScratchRoot() {
147	        guard package == nil else { return }
148	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: folderURL)
149	    }
150	}

1	// app/Sources/GraphicStore+Manual.swift — the graphics reference written
2	// into a package's `graphics/` (road map 10's G4a): `API.md` and `API.d.ts`,
3	// copies of the app's bundled `GraphicsAPI.md` and `GraphicsAPI.d.ts`, so an
4	// agent or a person editing the folder has the API beside the modules.
5	//
6	// **The manual is never a reason to create `graphics/`** (spec §11 G-14):
7	// `writeManual()` writes nothing unless the folder already exists, and
8	// `holdsContent` does not count the manual, so an untitled root holding only
9	// the manual is not carried by a save.
10	
11	import Foundation
12	
13	extension GraphicStore {
14	    /// What the manual is called inside `graphics/`.
15	    static let manualNames = ["API.md", "API.d.ts"]
16	    /// What it is called in the app's Resources, in `manualNames`' order.
17	    static let bundledManualNames = ["GraphicsAPI.md", "GraphicsAPI.d.ts"]
18	
19	    /// The directory holding `Fonts/`, which holds the manual too. The
20	    /// harness copies the manual there; the probes copy none, so for them
21	    /// `writeManual()` is a no-op.
22	    static func manualDirectory(besideFonts fonts: URL) -> URL {
23	        fonts.deletingLastPathComponent()
24	    }
25	
26	    var manualDirectory: URL { Self.manualDirectory(besideFonts: bundledFonts) }
27	
28	    /// The app bundle's own `GraphicsAPI.md`, no document involved:
29	    /// `graphic_reference` answers it and Help ▸ Graphics Reference opens it.
30	    static var bundledReferenceURL: URL {
31	        manualDirectory(besideFonts: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory)
32	            .appendingPathComponent(bundledManualNames[0])
33	    }
34	
35	    /// Main. Nothing unless `folderURL` exists; each file written
36	    /// (`.atomic`) only when its bytes differ from the bundled one; a
37	    /// bundled file that is absent is skipped silently.
38	    func writeManual() {
39	        let files = FileManager.default
40	        guard files.fileExists(atPath: folderURL.path) else { return }
41	        for (bundled, name) in zip(Self.bundledManualNames, Self.manualNames) {
42	            guard let bytes = try? Data(
43	                contentsOf: manualDirectory.appendingPathComponent(bundled))
44	            else { continue }
45	            let target = folderURL.appendingPathComponent(name)
46	            if let current = try? Data(contentsOf: target), current == bytes { continue }
47	            try? bytes.write(to: target, options: .atomic)
48	        }
49	    }
50	
51	    /// True when `folder` holds ANY entry, file or directory, that is
52	    /// neither hidden, one of `manualNames`, nor a `.partial`. A `fonts/` or
53	    /// `assets/` subfolder counts; `listing(_:)`'s regular-files rule is not
54	    /// this.
55	    static func holdsContent(_ folder: URL) -> Bool {
56	        let entries = (try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(
57	            at: folder, includingPropertiesForKeys: nil,
58	            options: [.skipsHiddenFiles])) ?? []
59	        return entries.contains {
60	            !manualNames.contains($0.lastPathComponent) && $0.pathExtension != "partial"
61	        }
62	    }
63	}

1	// app/Sources/GraphicScan.swift — what `GraphicStore` found in a package's
2	// `graphics/` folder: a module file, a font or asset file, and one pass's
3	// scan (road map 10 §5f, G3a). A pure move out of `GraphicStore.swift`.
4	
5	import CryptoKit
6	import Foundation
7	
8	/// One module file: its name (the file's stem), its bytes and its revision,
9	/// the SHA-256 of the bytes as 64 lowercase hex digits (G-13).
10	struct GraphicModuleFile: Equatable {
11	    let name: String, url: URL, bytes: Data, revision: String
12	}
13	
14	/// One font or asset file; `name` is its last path component.
15	struct GraphicFile: Equatable {
16	    let name: String, url: URL, bytes: Data
17	}
18	
19	/// What one pass over the folder found.
20	struct GraphicScan: Equatable {
21	    let modules: [String: GraphicModuleFile]
22	    let fonts: [GraphicFile], assets: [GraphicFile]
23	    /// The SHA-256 over the fonts then the assets, each name then bytes, in
24	    /// name order. The empty set hashes nothing.
25	    let libraryVersion: String
26	    /// A file the scan skipped, or a source it could not watch, in its own
27	    /// sentence.
28	    let warnings: [String]
29	
30	    static let empty = GraphicScan.empty(warnings: [])
31	
32	    /// Nothing found, with `warnings`: a package whose source did not arm.
33	    static func empty(warnings: [String]) -> GraphicScan {
34	        GraphicScan(
35	            modules: [:], fonts: [], assets: [],
36	            libraryVersion: GraphicStore.hex(SHA256().finalize()), warnings: warnings)
37	    }
